exposure.needed: which keys cert-manager signs with are 3072- or 4096-bit RSA keys, since the signing key length (e.g. CA issuer keys) is not carried as a declarative setting in the manifests the engine reads

consequence.statement: Certificates signed with larger RSA keys will be signed using SHA-384 (3072-bit keys) or SHA-512 (4096-bit keys) instead of always SHA-256; the release notes expect minimal impact beyond a slight increase in security and better compliance and are not aware of Kubernetes-based environments which support RSA 2048 and SHA-256 but fail with RSA 4096 and SHA-512.
consequence.remediation: If you use larger RSA keys, verify that clients and systems consuming the issued certificates accept SHA-384/SHA-512 signatures.

assertion.statement: In cert-manager v1.17.0 the hash algorithm used when signing with RSA is chosen based on the RSA key length — 3072-bit keys use SHA-384 and 4096-bit keys use SHA-512 — instead of always using SHA-256 as before, matching the existing ECDSA behavior.
